accepted.s: Who among the following was associated with the suppression of the uprising at Paralakimidi in the Ganjam region during the Revolt of 1857?
accepted.x: Captain Wilson suppressed the uprising led by Radhakrishna Dandasena at Paralakimidi and Dandasena was subsequently hanged.
accepted.tq: Match the person with the deed rather than with a nearby military name.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of 1857 → area of operation

accepted.s: Radhakrishna Dandasena led a revolt in which of the following places during 1857?
accepted.x: Radhakrishna Dandasena led the Girijan revolt at Paralakimidi in Ganjam, now in Gajapati district of Odisha.
accepted.tq: Use the area-of-operation clue to distinguish similarly placed Andhra and South Indian leaders.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of 1857 → area of operation

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Korukonda Subba Reddy:
1. He operated in Errannagudem in the Godavari Agency.
2. His rising was influenced by rumours about Nana Saheb's army.
3. He was released after being arrested by the British.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Subba Reddy was captured and executed, not released.
accepted.tq: Find the single false outcome statement among otherwise related facts.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of 1857 → area of operation

accepted.s: Who assisted the British in putting down the rising led by Korukonda Subba Reddy?
accepted.x: Buttaigudem Munsab Shankar Swamy helped the British suppress Korukonda Subba Reddy's rising in the Godavari Agency.
accepted.tq: Test the local collaborator associated with a particular uprising.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of 1857 → area of operation

accepted.s: Jamedar Chida Khan was connected with which of the following incidents during the Revolt of 1857?
o: The looting of the treasury at Jaggayyapeta
The attack on the British Residency at Hyderabad to secure his release
The raising of a green flag at Machilipatnam
accepted.x: Jamedar Chida Khan was imprisoned, and the attack on the British Residency at Hyderabad was intended to free him.
accepted.tq: Link the named individual with the specific incident rather than the location alone.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of 1857 → area of operation

accepted.s: On 28 August 1857, Sheikh Peer Sahib of Cuddapah was reported to have
o: attacked the British Residency at Hyderabad
preached jihad and prayed for the success of the Mughal Emperor
raised a green flag at Machilipatnam
accepted.x: Sheikh Peer Sahib preached jihad at Cuddapah on 28 August 1857 and prayed for the success of the Mughal Emperor; he was later arrested.
accepted.tq: Combine the date with the precise action to separate closely related 1857 incidents.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of 1857 → area of operation

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Radhakrishna Dandasena was associated with Paralakimidi in Ganjam. Nanded was among the other Hyderabad-State areas affected by risings.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly paired person and area from a cluster of nearby 1857 associations.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of 1857 → area of operation

accepted.s: The rising led by Mir Fida Ali in June 1857 was suppressed by
accepted.x: Mir Fida Ali's rising at Aurangabad in June 1857 was suppressed by Captain Abbat, and Mir Fida Ali was hanged.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the suppressing officer from commanders connected with other revolts.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of 1857 → area of operation

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding incidents in the Andhra region during the Revolt of 1857 is correct?
o: A Telugu placard at Visakhapatnam called for renaming the town Mohammed Pattanam.
The treasury at Jaggayyapeta was used to store weapons for the Company.
A green flag was raised at Machilipatnam in support of the British Crown.
The unrest was confined to Visakhapatnam and did not spread to Narsipatnam.
accepted.x: A Telugu placard displayed at Visakhapatnam during Muharram called for renaming the town Mohammed Pattanam. The Jaggayyapeta treasury was looted, and unrest also spread to Narsipatnam.
accepted.tq: Reject reversed or exaggerated descriptions of separate local incidents.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of 1857 → area of operation

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the Hyderabad-State areas associated with risings during 1857?
accepted.x: Sholapur, Chanda and Nanded were among the Hyderabad-State areas associated with risings. Machilipatnam was an Andhra coastal centre where a green flag was raised and prayers were offered for the Mughal Emperor.
accepted.tq: Separate the listed Hyderabad-State areas from a similarly connected coastal Andhra town.
accepted.sec: Andhra leaders of 1857 → area of operation

accepted.s: The Rampa Rebellion of 1879–80 was primarily directed against
o: the imprisonment of Jamedar Chida Khan
the disbanding of the Vizianagaram troops
the Permanent Settlement imposed on Narayana Babu
Munsubar Madhava Bhupati Dev and oppressive taxation
accepted.x: The 1879–80 Rampa Rebellion in the Rampachodavaram Agency opposed Munsubar Madhava Bhupati Dev and oppressive taxes. Madhava Bhupati Dev had been appointed in 1848.
accepted.tq: Identify the immediate cause and official targeted by the uprising.
accepted.sec: Rampa and Godavari agency risings

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events connected with the Rampa Rebellion of 1879 in chronological order:
A. Madhava Bhupati Dev was appointed Munsubar.
B. The Vaddagudem police station was raided.
C. The Rekapalle rising was suppressed.
D. The broader Rampa rising was crushed.
accepted.x: Madhava Bhupati Dev was appointed in 1848; Vaddagudem police station was raided on 10 July 1879; the Rekapalle rising was suppressed in September 1879; and the broader Rampa rising was crushed by November 1880.
accepted.tq: Use the fixed dates and the final suppression to establish first, middle and last.
accepted.sec: Rampa and Godavari agency risings

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the Rampa and Godavari Agency risings?
accepted.x: Ambul Reddy led the Rekapalle rising and also figured among the leaders of the wider 1879–80 Rampa Rebellion.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure leader–uprising pair and eliminate unrelated episodes.
accepted.sec: Rampa and Godavari agency risings

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Rekapalle rising:
1. It occurred in Bhadrachalam taluk.
2. It was connected with an increase in the axe tax on podu.
3. The Vaddagudem police station was raided on 10 July 1879.
4. It was suppressed in September 1879.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Rekapalle rising occurred in Bhadrachalam taluk, followed an increase in the podu axe tax, included the raid on Vaddagudem police station on 10 July 1879, and was suppressed in September 1879.
accepted.tq: Check each chronological and numerical detail before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Rampa and Godavari agency risings

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the two Rampa rebellions?
o: The 1879–80 rebellion was associated with Alluri Sitarama Raju, whereas the 1922–24 rebellion was led by Madhava Bhupati Dev.
The 1922–24 rebellion preceded the 1879–80 rebellion and was led by Ambul Reddy.
The 1879–80 rebellion was led by local agency leaders, whereas the 1922–24 rebellion was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.
Both rebellions were led by Alluri Sitarama Raju and occurred in the same period.
accepted.x: The 1879–80 Rampa Rebellion was led by local figures including Chandrayya, Tammanna Dora, Pulikantha Sambaiah and Ambul Reddy. Alluri Sitarama Raju led the later 1922–24 Rampa Rebellion.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar names and dates instead of transferring the famous leader to the earlier revolt.
accepted.sec: Rampa and Godavari agency risings

accepted.s: The British officer associated with the command of the Company forces at the Battle of Padmanabham was
accepted.x: Colonel Pendergast commanded the English East India Company forces at the Battle of Padmanabham.
accepted.tq: Match the military commander with the correct battle, avoiding names from other suppressive operations.
accepted.sec: Vizianagaram vs the Company - Battle of Padmanabham (1794)

accepted.s: What immediate demand of the East India Company was refused by Chinna Vijayarama Raju before the Battle of Padmanabham?
o: Payment of a six-lakh-rupee peshkash under the Permanent Settlement
Transfer of the Vizianagaram estate to three Hyderabad officials
Payment of a three-lakh-rupee tribute and disbanding of his troops
Surrender of the Cuddapah fort and release of political prisoners
accepted.x: The Company demanded a tribute of Rs 3 lakh and the disbanding of the Raja's troops. Chinna Vijayarama Raju refused these demands.
accepted.tq: Separate the pre-battle demand from the later six-lakh-rupee settlement condition.
accepted.sec: Vizianagaram vs the Company - Battle of Padmanabham (1794)

accepted.s: On 2 August 1793, the British took which of the following actions in relation to Vizianagaram?
o: They seized the fort, divided the estate into three parts and ordered the Raja to reside at Machilipatnam on a pension.
They restored the estate to Narayana Babu under the Permanent Settlement.
They appointed Madhava Bhupati Dev as Munsubar of Rampachodavaram.
They defeated the Raja at Padmanabham and killed over a thousand warriors.
accepted.x: On 2 August 1793, the British seized the Vizianagaram fort, divided the estate into three parts and ordered the Raja to reside at Machilipatnam on a pension of Rs 1,200.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the dated preliminary action rather than the later battle outcome.
accepted.sec: Vizianagaram vs the Company - Battle of Padmanabham (1794)

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Chinna Vijayarama Raju is correct?
1. He ruled Vizianagaram from 1760 to 1794.
2. He removed his step-brother and Diwan Sitarama Raju for misrule in 1784.
3. Sitarama Raju later regained his post by bribing members of the Council.
4. The peshkash subsequently fell into arrears.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. These developments formed the background to the Company's conflict with the Vizianagaram Raja.
accepted.tq: Verify the complete chain of background facts, including the less prominent administrative detail.
accepted.sec: Vizianagaram vs the Company - Battle of Padmanabham (1794)

accepted.s: The Battle of Padmanabham was fought between the English East India Company and
o: the Pusapati Vizianagaram zamindar Chinna Vijayarama Gajapati Raju II
the Munsubar of Rampachodavaram supported by the Rohillas
the Nizam's forces led by Turrebaz Khan
the Raja of Bobbili supported by Nana Saheb
accepted.x: The battle was fought between the English East India Company and Pusapati Chinna Vijayarama Gajapati Raju II, the Vizianagaram zamindar.
accepted.tq: Use the parties to the conflict to distinguish Padmanabham from other Andhra and Hyderabad episodes.
accepted.sec: Vizianagaram vs the Company - Battle of Padmanabham (1794)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the political result of the Battle of Padmanabham?
o: The estate was permanently annexed without any restoration to the ruling family.
The estate was merged with the Godavari Agency under the Munsubar system.
Vizianagaram was reduced to an ordinary zamindari and later restored to Narayana Babu under conditions.
Vizianagaram became an independent kingdom free from Company control.
accepted.x: After the British victory, Vizianagaram was reduced to an ordinary zamindari. The minor son Narayana Babu later regained it subject to the Permanent Settlement and payment of peshkash.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the immediate political reduction from the later conditional restoration.
accepted.sec: Vizianagaram vs the Company - Battle of Padmanabham (1794)

accepted.s: Narayana Babu, the minor son of Chinna Vijayarama Raju, was associated with which of the following places before the restoration of the Vizianagaram estate?
accepted.x: Narayana Babu had hidden at Makkuva before receiving the Vizianagaram estate back under the Permanent Settlement.
accepted.tq: Separate the hiding place of the heir from the place where the Raja was ordered to reside.
accepted.sec: Vizianagaram vs the Company - Battle of Padmanabham (1794)

accepted.s: The restoration of the Vizianagaram estate to Narayana Babu was made subject to
o: the payment of a three-lakh-rupee tribute and abolition of zamindari
the disbanding of all Company troops and a four-lakh-rupee grant
the appointment of George Russell as the hereditary zamindar
the Permanent Settlement of 1802 and payment of a six-lakh-rupee peshkash
accepted.x: Narayana Babu received the estate under the Permanent Settlement of 1802 and was required to pay a peshkash of Rs 6 lakh.
accepted.tq: Contrast the three-lakh demand before the battle with the six-lakh post-restoration peshkash.
accepted.sec: Vizianagaram vs the Company - Battle of Padmanabham (1794)

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: George Russell — special officer over the forts
Culloden — comparison used for the Battle of Padmanabham
Madhava Bhupati Dev — British commander at Padmanabham
accepted.x: Madhava Bhupati Dev was the Munsubar against whom the 1879–80 Rampa Rebellion was directed. George Russell was made special officer over the Vizianagaram forts, and Padmanabham was compared to Culloden.
accepted.tq: Spot the swapped official and battle commander from otherwise correct associations.
accepted.sec: Vizianagaram vs the Company - Battle of Padmanabham (1794)
